<research_package>

## Research question
Does adding Method M to existing white-box knowledge-distillation losses improve the instruction-following quality of distilled student models, consistently across KD losses and evaluation sets, and which of its components drive the change?

## Methods summary
Method M is a plug-in curriculum for knowledge distillation of LLMs. A difficulty measurer ranks training samples by fusing two rankings (ROUGE-L of the student's output against the reference, and the student's cross-entropy) with reciprocal rank fusion, then splits them into 4 subsets from easy to hard. A scheduler adds one subset per stage, while the distillation temperature rises linearly from 1 to 2 and, for off-policy losses, the weight of the supervised loss decays from 0.3 to 0. It is combined with existing KD losses (e.g., KLD, GKD, SRKL) and compared with the same losses without it, plus SFT and SeqKD baselines.

## Experimental setup
Teacher GPT-2 1.5B fine-tuned on databricks-dolly-15K (12.5K train / 1K validation / 0.5K test after filtering); students are GPT-2 120M models distilled with each method for the same number of iterations, hyperparameters chosen on validation ROUGE-L. Evaluation on five instruction-following sets (DollyEval, SelfInst, VicunaEval, S-NI, UnNI) with ROUGE-L. Responses are sampled at temperature 1 and scores are averaged over five generations per prompt with five random seeds; the number of independent training runs is not stated.

## Experiments and comparisons
- `exp1`: Plug-in evaluation across KD losses, GPT-2 family (T1)
  - comparison `exp1/cmp1`: Each KD loss with vs without Method M, per dataset and on average
  - comparison `exp1/cmp2`: Best distilled students vs the teacher
- `exp2`: Component ablation with KLD (T2)
  - comparison `exp2/cmp1`: Full Method M vs variants without the temperature schedule and/or the supervised-ratio schedule, and vs plain KLD

sentences.text: Adding Method M to each of the three evaluated KD losses (GKD, KLD, SRKL) improved average ROUGE-L across the five instruction-following sets, with gains of 2.33, 1.60, and 1.51 points, respectively, and also improved scores on most individual datasets.

The component ablation with KLD shows that the supervised-ratio schedule is the main driver of the improvement: removing it (keeping only the temperature schedule) yields scores close to or below plain KLD (e.g., DollyEval 22.04 vs 23.49, SelfInst 8.70 vs 10.33), whereas removing the temperature schedule (keeping the ratio schedule) retains most of the gain (e.g., DollyEval 24.33, UnNI 23.87).

The best distilled student with Method M (SRKL + Method M) outperformed the teacher on two of five datasets (VicunaEval 16.66 vs 16.47, S-NI 28.49 vs 27.66) but not on the other three or on average (22.94 vs 23.44).

No statistical tests or standard deviations are reported, so the significance and consistency of these gains cannot be established, and the findings are limited to the GPT-2 family and the five evaluated instruction-following sets.

Adding Method M to each of the three evaluated KD losses (GKD, KLD, SRKL) improved average ROUGE-L across the five instruction-following sets, with gains of 2.33, 1.60, and 1.51 points respectively, and the improvement was consistent on every individual dataset for each loss.

The ablation with KLD shows that the full Method M (with both the rising temperature and the decaying supervised-loss ratio) yields the highest scores on all five datasets, while removing the ratio schedule (keeping only the temperature schedule) reduces performance on four of five datasets, and removing both schedules (keeping only the easy-to-hard curriculum) performs comparably to plain KLD on average.

These results are limited to the GPT-2 family, the three KD losses and five evaluation sets tested, and no statistical significance tests were reported, so the consistency and size of the improvements cannot be formally established.

Adding Method M to each of the three evaluated KD losses (GKD, KLD, SRKL) improved average ROUGE-L across the five instruction-following sets, with gains of 2.33, 1.60, and 1.51 points respectively, and the improvement was observed on every individual dataset for each loss.

The ablation with KLD shows that the full Method M (with both the rising temperature and the decaying supervised-loss ratio) yields the highest scores on all five datasets, while removing the ratio schedule (keeping only the temperature schedule) reduces performance on all five datasets, and removing both schedules (keeping only the easy-to-hard curriculum) performs comparably to plain KLD on average.

These results are limited to the GPT-2 1.5B-to-0.1B setting, the three KD losses and five evaluation sets tested, and no statistical significance tests were reported, so the consistency and size of the improvements cannot be formally established.
